resources.string: The laptop talks to the sleeve and keeps the recordings. This phone shows them over Wi-Fi. Phone and laptop must be on the same Wi-Fi.
Searching this Wi-Fi for HAVen. This takes a few seconds.
The laptop you used last time.
Tap it to open the dashboard.
Check that the laptop is on and HAVen is running on it, and that both are on the same Wi-Fi. Then search again, or open “Can’t connect?” below.
Could not search this network (%1$s). Open “Can’t connect?” below and type the address.
Tap it to open the dashboard again, or search for another laptop.
1. Put the phone and the laptop on the same Wi-Fi.\n2. On the laptop, start HAVen for phones (the person who set up the laptop can do this):

3. If the laptop asks whether Python may accept incoming connections, choose Allow.\n\nSome networks keep devices apart (eduroam, guest or company Wi-Fi). Then use a phone hotspot or a separate router.
Shown on the laptop under Wi-Fi settings, for example 192.168.1.23. Add the port if it is not 8000.
Type the laptop’s address, for example 192.168.1.23 or 192.168.1.23:8000.
The laptop did not answer. Is it on, with HAVen running, on the same Wi-Fi as this phone?
Something answered at that address, but it is not HAVen.
The laptop refused this phone. HAVen on the laptop needs to be started for phones: see “Can’t connect?” below.
Try every screen with made-up data that runs on this phone. Nothing in it is a measurement from a person.
Not a medical device. Vibration is unweighted (not ISO 5349); grip effort is relative to each wearer’s calibration, not force.
Could not load %1$s (%2$s). The laptop may be off, asleep or on another Wi-Fi.
%1$s is a HAVen backend but does not serve the dashboard (was it started with --dashboard none?).
This backend was started with a password (VG_BASIC_AUTH). It is kept only while the app is open.
Sign-in cancelled. The dashboard needs the user name and password the backend was started with.
